newsitem.title: USA: Schering-Plough sees $5 bln in 96 drug sales.
newsitem.headline: Schering-Plough sees $5 bln in 96 drug sales.

text.p: Schering-Plough Corp said on Thursday that it expects sales for its pharmaceutical divisions, including animal health, to total $5.0 billion in 1996.
The drug sales would top the company's 1995 worldwide pharmaceutical sales of $4.5 billion.

In a statement summarizing comments by a senior executive at a meeting of health care industry analysts, Schering-Plough said the company expected sales of its Claritin non-sedating antihistimine to top $1.0 billion this year. The drug sold $789 worldwide in 1995.
Raul Cesan, president of Schering-Plough's pharmaceutical division, told the meeting the company expects Claritin to gain marketing clearance in Japan in the second half of 1997.
The company's research and development spending is expected at around $720 million in 1996, up from $657 million in 1995.
Schering-Plough expects to file for U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of interleukin-10 for treating Crohn's disease, an inflammatory bowel condition, by year-end 1997, Cesan said.
